text.insert: The script installs Docker, opens ports 22, 80 and 443 (TCP, plus UDP 443 for HTTP/3), adds a 2 GB swapfile, clones the repository to
, and builds the image. It also creates an
user with Docker access but no sudo, and copies your SSH key to it. Use the default cloud user or root for system maintenance.
Setup takes 5 to 8 minutes and writes

ssh archon@your-server-ip
nano /opt/archon/.env          # see "Configure .env" below
cd /opt/archon
docker compose --profile with-db --profile cloud up -d
Run Archon on your own machine with SQLite and the Web UI. No domain or VPS is needed.

git clone https://github.com/coleam00/Archon.git
cd Archon
cp .env.example .env           # set a Claude or Codex credential
docker compose up -d

Published images carry BuildKit provenance and SPDX SBOM attestations. Resolve the tag to a digest, then inspect that digest so the image cannot change between inspection and deployment:

docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/coleam00/archon:latest
# Copy the top-level Digest, not a platform manifest's digest.
image='ghcr.io/coleam00/archon@sha256:<digest>'
docker buildx imagetools inspect "$image" --format '{{ json .Provenance }}'
docker buildx imagetools inspect "$image" --format '{{ json .SBOM }}'
Both results must be non-empty: each platform has a

and the revision is the release commit you intend to run. Current releases record them in

Root fallback for macOS bind mounts
On a macOS bind mount (VirtioFS), the ownership fix always fails: the host will not remap files to UID 1001. The entrypoint prints the
error and exits 1, so the container restarts in a loop. Read-only mounts and SELinux or AppArmor denials on Linux fail the same way.

An installed, verified Slack plugin stays as it is, including a release you pinned from another source. The image does not update it.

Missing or changed Slack executables, ownership conflicts, or a broken image receipt when a new install is needed stop provisioning with an error in the boot logs. Repair the install before restarting.
To turn Slack off, remove its tokens from every env source, run
docker compose exec -u appuser app bun run cli plugin remove coleam00/Archon/plugins/chat-slack
, and restart. Removing only the plugin reinstalls it on the next start. Removing only the tokens leaves it installed and reporting missing credentials.

Mounting the Docker socket into the app container is not part of the supported stack. The socket is root-equivalent: anything that can reach it can start a privileged container and take over the host. If you accept that on a single-operator host, read
without that risk, run Archon directly on a host with a local Docker daemon.

docker build -t archon .
docker run --env-file .env -e ARCHON_DOCKER=true -p 3000:3000 archon
